main_body: Beehive-shaped thatched hut: a large conical thatch roof (rows 3-56) over a short clay-brick wall with an arched doorway (rows 57-77)
top_band: Golden thatch dome, rows ~3-56, banded courses from light yellow to dark brown. It reads as a roof slope seen from above, with the ridge courses at the top.
evidence: Down the middle column: the thatch roof is a large sloped top surface with many courses and a dark lower eave edge at rows ~54-56. Directly below is a shaded band under the eave (rows 57-60), then the clay wall face down to a stone base. The doorway has a wooden frame and a dark inset interior, and the roof arch is cut into the thatch. The roof clearly shows its top slope, as on the reference houses. There is no receding side face.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 tones with per-course highlights, dark gap lines and straw ticks. The wall has brick-like dashes, mottled shading and a speckled stone base. Outlines are dark brown, tinted to the neighbouring material rather than near-black. There are no large flat fills, and tile density is comparable to the references.
